topics.topic: The Rogue Planet Wandering the Milky Way
topics.hook: Right now, there is an untethered planet the size of Jupiter hurtling through dark space with no star to call home.
topics.why_watch: Taps into existential curiosity, cosmic dread, and the vast scale of space. Visually stunning and easy to illustrate using public NASA footage or CGI.

topics.topic: The False Memory Experiment (Mandela Effect at Scale)
topics.hook: Think you have a solid memory? Let me prove to you that your brain has already fabricated hundreds of memories you swear are real.
topics.why_watch: Direct audience participation drives massive comment-section debate, high retention rate, and rapid sharing among friends testing each other.

topics.topic: The Creature That Can Reset Its Age to Zero
topics.hook: There is an animal on Earth that can literally reverse its own aging process and live forever.
topics.why_watch: Biological superpowers defy standard human logic about death and aging, creating instant curiosity and rewatch value.

topics.topic: What If Earth Lost Oxygen for Just 5 Seconds?
topics.hook: If Earth lost all oxygen for just 5 seconds, daytime would turn pitch black, and every untreated concrete structure would instantly crumble to dust.
topics.why_watch: High-stakes 'what if' scenarios trigger instant visualization of catastrophic consequences, keeping retention high until the end.

topics.topic: The Undersea Cables Powering 99% of the Global Internet
topics.hook: Almost nothing you do online goes through satellites. It actually travels through garden-hose-sized cables sitting at the bottom of the ocean.
topics.why_watch: Shatters a widespread misconception about daily technology; visually striking maps and vulnerability facts (like shark bites and anchor strikes) keep viewers hooked.

topics.topic: The Loudest Sound Ever Recorded in Human History
topics.hook: In 1883, a sound on Earth was so powerful it ruptured eardrums 40 miles away and circled the entire planet four times.
topics.why_watch: Extreme world-record events create dramatic storytelling; sound design possibilities make the reel naturally immersive.

topics.hook: For a thousand years, historians dismissed this ancient metropolis as a myth—until a diver stumbled across 16-foot statues under the sea.
topics.why_watch: Real-life 'Atlantis' discovery brings ancient history to life, combining adventure, underwater exploration, and historical mystery.

topics.topic: The Sperm Whale's Deadly Sonic Weapon
topics.hook: A sperm whale's click is so loud that if you swam too close, the sound wave could literally vibrate your body to death.
topics.why_watch: Combines deep-sea mystery with an unbelievable animal superpower; creates intense acoustic curiosity.

topics.topic: The Tetris Effect: How Screens Rewire Your Dreams
topics.hook: Ever played a game or scrolled so long that you saw it behind your eyelids when you closed your eyes? Here's what your brain is actually doing.
topics.why_watch: Hyper-relatable everyday experience for modern screen users, backed by legitimate neuroscience explaining cognitive plasticity.

topics.topic: The Antikythera Mechanism: The World's First Analog Computer
topics.hook: Over 2,000 years ago, ancient Greeks built a geared mechanical computer so complex that humanity wouldn't match it again for another 1,400 years.
topics.why_watch: Challenges modern assumptions about ancient technology and historical progress; features mysterious bronze artifacts that immediately look cinematic.
